briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Rescheduling Momentum Builds Nationally as Michigan Operators Eye a Path Through the Wholesale Tax
briefs.top: Federal reform has real teeth this week — DEA's own lawyers are now on the record urging Schedule III, and psychedelic medicine notched fresh wins from Compass Pathways' six-month data to a new VA-backed veterans trial. Back home, Michigan operators are pushing back on the 24% wholesale tax with a September trial date and a governor's-race repeal pledge, while brands keep launching product into a market still moving serious volume.

local.text: Choice Labs is rebranding as "Intrinsic" this month, scrubbing old packaging across its line but keeping its top-selling gummy — proof MI brands are still innovating even under tax pressure.
The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's newest lawsuit against the 24% wholesale tax gives operators a fresh shot at relief, with the case heading to trial in September.
The wholesale tax is now a governor's-race issue: Democratic candidate Chris Swanson has vowed to repeal it if elected, giving the industry a real political lifeline heading toward November.
Flower just hit a new floor — the average ounce sold for $58 in June, the cheapest ever in Michigan — a win for consumer demand even as it squeezes margins.

TerrAscend has completed $79M in debt financing to exit Michigan, and Ann Arbor storefronts like Arbors Wellness and Leaf & Bud have shut down — thinning the herd and freeing up shelf space and market share for the independents left standing.

national.text: DEA formally urged its administrative law judge to recommend moving marijuana from Schedule I to Schedule III, arguing the evidence from the nearly three-week hearing shows the drug no longer meets Schedule I's requirements — a major green light as the judge finalizes his recommendation.

DEA released the full 2,533-page transcript of its rescheduling hearing, capturing government lawyers making the case that marijuana "can no longer remain in Schedule I" — a paper trail strengthening the push toward Schedule III.

Compass Pathways' six-month COMP006 data confirmed a rapid, durable response from synthetic psilocybin COMP360 in treatment-resistant depression, and the company still plans to submit its FDA new drug application in Q4 2026 — keeping psychedelic medicine on track for a real launch.

Compass Pathways is donating its drug to a new VA-run trial, PIVOT, testing COMP360 psilocybin in veterans with treatment-resistant depression and PTSD — a rare case of the federal government actively partnering on psychedelic research.

M&A is picking up: Vireo Growth's run of acquisitions — including Cannabist's multistate assets and Planet 13 — has it on track to become the largest U.S. cannabis retailer by store count, proof consolidation can still mint scaled winners.
